newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen calls for free and fair election.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen calls for free and fair election.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said on Sunday, a week after ousting his senior rival, that the country must have a free and fair election.
"It is necessary...to ensure a free and fair general election, which is the aim of all of us," he said in statement read by an announcer on national radio. He gave no date for the election.

Last month Hun Sen agreed with First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, the man he later ousted in two days of bloody fighting in Phnom Penh, that a general election should be held next May 23, exactly five years after U.N.-organised polls that led to their coalition.

Hun Sen also called on all Cambodian newspapers, including those critical of him, to resume publication. "As for the press, including newspapers that used to be critical, please hurry and publish," his statement said.

Some Cambodian newspapers, including many that supported Ranariddh, ceased publication during the two days of fighting and subsequent chaos. Many members of Ranariddh's party as well as foreign business people and aid workers fled the country in the aftermath of the prince's ouster.
Major foreign governments have condemned the violence and some have suspended or are reconsidering their aid programmes.
